title: What training is mandatory for employers in Australia?
description: Mandatory employer training in Australia by theme: WHS, harassment, privacy and security, AML/CTF, financial services, licensing and CPD, care and transport.
shortAnswer: As at November 2026, every Australian employer must provide the information, training, instruction and supervision needed to protect people from work risks under work health and safety laws, and must take reasonable measures to prevent sexual harassment. Beyond that, training duties depend on sector and state: AML/CTF programs, financial adviser CPD, aged care and NDIS standards, licenses for high risk, security, liquor and gambling work, and annual security awareness in Commonwealth entities.
keyTakeaways: Australia layers Commonwealth law, model WHS laws adopted everywhere except Victoria, and state licensing regimes, so the same role can carry different training duties in Sydney and Melbourne.

The general WHS duty sets no interval; fixed cycles come from specific instruments, such as annual security awareness under the ISM and PSPF and annual incident and complaints training under the Aged Care Rules.
Licenses drive much of the cycle: high risk work licenses expire after 5 years, NSW RSA and gambling cards are refreshed every 5 years, and Victorian RSA every 3 years.

Professional CPD runs on different years: 40 hours for financial advisers, 10 units for solicitors (1 April to 31 March in NSW), 40 credits for pharmacists (year ending 30 September), and 120 hours over 3 years for tax agents.

2025 to 2027 changes include AML/CTF reform for lawyers, accountants and real estate from 1 July 2026, the new Aged Care Act Rules, national child safety training from February 2026, and Victorian estate agent CPD from April 2027.

sections.heading: How are mandatory training duties set in Australia?

blocks.text: Australian training duties come from three sources that overlap: Commonwealth law (financial services, AML/CTF, privacy, aged care, NDIS, aviation, Commonwealth security), work health and safety law (the model WHS laws in the Commonwealth and every state and territory except Victoria, and Victoria's own OHS Act), and state and territory licensing for trades, security, liquor, gambling, food, child safety and the professions. An employer with sites in several states needs a register that holds all three.

The general WHS duty is the base layer. Section 19(3)(f) of the WHS Act requires the provision of any information, training, instruction or supervision necessary to protect all persons from risks arising from work, and the regulations require that training be suitable and adequate and readily understandable ([Work Health and Safety Act 2011](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2011A00137/latest/text)). Officers must exercise due diligence, including taking reasonable steps to verify that those resources and processes are provided and used (section 27(5)(f)). None of this sets an interval; specific regulations and codes do, for particular hazards.

Many expectations sit in ASIC regulatory guides, industry codes and model codes of practice rather than statute. The tables below cover every Australian regulation page in this library, as at November 2026, and mark where a duty is guidance. The [United States hub](/guides/mandatory-workplace-training-in-the-united-states) shows a similar federal and state split.

sections.heading: What work health and safety training must Australian employers provide?

blocks.text: Every person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU) must provide the training needed to manage work risks, and specific regulations add training for hazards such as asbestos, confined spaces, falls and construction. High risk work, construction induction, traffic control and statutory mining roles also need a license, card or certificate before work starts.

blocks.text: Victoria runs a parallel system: its construction induction card lapses after 2 years without construction work ([Victorian OHS Regulations, r 349](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/17-22sra018-authorised.pdf)), while the model white card never expires but triggers retraining after the same gap (r 316). Many intervals also live in codes rather than regulations: the first aid code's annual CPR refresher and three yearly requalification are guidance ([Safe Work Australia](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/sites/default/files/2021-10/code_of_practice_-_first_aid_in_the_workplace_July%202019.pdf)).

sections.heading: What harassment, whistleblowing and conduct training is required?

blocks.text: Every Australian employer has a positive duty under the Sex Discrimination Act to take reasonable and proportionate measures to eliminate sexual harassment, and the Australian Human Rights Commission says one off induction training is ineffective unless reinforced. Public and large proprietary companies must have a whistleblower policy, and companies face a failure to prevent foreign bribery offence with an adequate procedures defense.

blocks.text: The Commission's guidelines list attendance records with a copy of the training content as evidence, and it has had compliance powers since 12 December 2023 ([Australian Human Rights Commission](https://humanrights.gov.au/__data/assets/file/0030/46974/Guidelines-for-Complying-with-the-Positive-Duty-2023.pdf)). For foreign bribery, the company carries the legal burden of proving adequate procedures, and the penalty is the greatest of 100,000 penalty units, three times the benefit or 10% of turnover ([Criminal Code, s 70.5A](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04868/latest/text)).

sections.heading: What privacy and security training applies in Australia?

blocks.text: Commonwealth agencies must provide privacy training at induction and take reasonable steps to provide it annually, and entities applying the Protective Security Policy Framework and Information Security Manual must provide security awareness training at engagement and annually. Private sector security training is mostly set through prudential standards, critical infrastructure rules and Defence industry membership.

Private organizations under the Privacy Act have no equivalent annual rule.

sections.heading: What AML/CTF training does Australian law require?

blocks.text: Reporting entities must have AML/CTF policies that deal with initial and ongoing training appropriate to each person's function and risks, under the AML/CTF Rules 2025. Lawyers, accountants, trust and company service providers, conveyancers and real estate businesses joined the regime from 1 July 2026.

The legal test in section 5-9 is appropriate, readily understandable training ([AML/CTF Rules 2025](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2025L01026/latest)).

sections.heading: What competence and training rules apply to financial services firms?

blocks.text: Financial services and credit licensees must ensure their representatives are adequately trained and competent, under section 912A(1)(f) of the Corporations Act and section 47(1)(g) of the National Credit Act. Only some regimes fix hours: 40 hours of CPD a year for financial advisers and 20 hours for third party home loan representatives.

sections.heading: Which licensed occupations and professions carry training or CPD cycles?

blocks.text: State licensing makes training a condition of working in security, liquor, gambling and the trades, usually with a refresher tied to license renewal. Professional bodies and boards set annual or triennial CPD for lawyers, accountants, tax agents and real estate agents, each on its own year.

sections.heading: What training do health, aged care, disability and food businesses need?

blocks.text: Registered health practitioners must complete CPD set by their national board to renew registration, and aged care and NDIS providers must train workers under their standards and rules. Hospitals are assessed against national safety and quality standards, and food businesses need food safety supervisors and trained handlers.

sections.heading: What training applies to transport and aviation workers?

blocks.text: Transport duties in Australia are set by national laws for heavy vehicles and rail, Commonwealth aviation and maritime rules, and state dangerous goods licensing. Several carry fixed recurrent cycles, such as drug and alcohol education every 30 months in aviation and continuation training every 24 months for aircraft maintenance staff.

sections.heading: How should an Australian employer build a single training register?

blocks.text: Build the register by jurisdiction first, then by license or registration, then by role. Australian duties attach to the state where the work happens (WHS, liquor, security, child safety), to the license a person holds (high risk work, RSA, CPD for professionals), and to the employer's regulated status (AFS licensee, reporting entity, registered provider), so a single national template misses obligations.

items: **Map every site to its WHS regime.** Model WHS law or Victoria's OHS Act, plus any state regulation such as NSW traffic control or Queensland electrical rescue.

**List the entity's regulated statuses.** AFS or credit licensee, AML/CTF reporting entity, APRA regulated entity, registered aged care or NDIS provider, Commonwealth entity under the PSPF, DISP member. Each brings its own training rule.

**Record each person's licenses and registrations with expiry dates.** High risk work licenses, RSA and RCG cards, security licenses, food safety supervisor certificates, practising certificates and Ahpra registration all run on personal cycles.

**Record each CPD year exactly.** Financial advisers (40 hours), solicitors (NSW year from 1 April), pharmacists (year ending 30 September), real estate (NSW year from 1 July), tax agents and accountants (triennial with annual minimums).

**Separate rules from guidance.** Mark whether an interval comes from law (ISM, PSPF, Aged Care Rules, CASR Part 99) or from a code, regulatory guide or regulator example (first aid code, AUSTRAC examples, RG 270). Where only guidance exists, record the risk rationale using [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

**Apply retention rules per instrument.** Asbestos training records 5 years after ceasing work, aviation drug and alcohol education 5 years, aged care worker records 7 years, RTO assessment records 2 years. See [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

blocks.text: Linking each row to its instrument lets the register answer an inspector or regulator directly. The [training matrix guide](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) covers the layout by role and topic, and [mapping training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) covers the link from each obligation to the learning outcome that satisfies it.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each obligation against its jurisdiction, instrument and type (law, code or guidance), so a multi-state employer can see which rule drives each learning outcome in each location. When a source changes, such as a new PSPF release or Aged Care Rules amendment, the affected outcomes and roles are identified directly. The [audit evidence](/platform/audit-evidence) page describes how this evidence is held.

faqs.q: Is there a legal requirement for annual compliance training in Australia?
faqs.a: Not generally. The WHS duty requires necessary training without an interval. Annual intervals appear in specific instruments: ISM and PSPF security awareness for Commonwealth entities, the Agencies Privacy Code, and Aged Care Rules training on incident, complaints and whistleblower systems. Other annual figures, such as AUSTRAC's examples or ASIC's whistleblower good practice, are guidance.

faqs.q: Do model codes of practice make training intervals mandatory?
faqs.a: A model code has legal effect only once a jurisdiction approves it, and even then it is evidence of what is known about a hazard rather than a rule. A PCBU can meet its duty another way if it provides an equivalent or higher standard. Intervals in codes, such as annual CPR refreshers, are therefore strong guidance.

faqs.q: When did AML/CTF training duties start for lawyers, accountants and real estate agents?
faqs.a: The AML/CTF reforms regulated trust and company service providers, lawyers, accountants, conveyancers and real estate businesses providing listed services from 1 July 2026. They must run personnel due diligence and role appropriate initial and ongoing training under the AML/CTF Rules 2025.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for a worker's license or CPD, the employer or the worker?
faqs.a: Usually both. The license or registration belongs to the individual, but employers must not let unlicensed people do licensed work, such as high risk work or alcohol service, and some regimes put the duty on the employer directly, such as the PCBU duty to provide white card training or verify Working with Children Checks.
